content.comment_body: Hello everyone, is there a way to periodically save the contents of [product_name] built-in datalogger to SD memory? The 2000 line limit is too restrictive for my application, and SD storage could be a solution. Thank you, [user_name]

If you insert an SD card and set [product_name] [article_no] to RUN mode, data will be written to the SD card. The maximum allowed by the datalogger is: - Internal memory: 200 lines - SD card: 2000 lines Each datalog file can hold up to 2000 lines on the SD card. If you transfer the datalog file to your computer and want to log further data to the SD card, you must switch [product_name] [article_no] to STOP mode and then back to RUN. This creates a new datalog file on the SD card with a different name. Hope this clarifies things.

Thank you for your response. I manage several sites equipped with [product_name] and visit approximately once a month. My requirement is for greater logging capacity—while the SD card provides this, the process needs to be automated. I'm looking for a function in the [product_name] program that can automatically restart the log with a new file name. Thanks again, [user_name]
A separate thread has been created for the topic: [article_no] how to write logs on SD memory. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user is limited by the [product_name] datalogger's file size restriction of 2000 lines per file on SD memory and wishes to automate logging beyond this limit. Currently, users must manually switch between STOP and RUN modes to start new log files, which poses challenges for remote or infrequently visited locations. The demand is for a continuous, automated logging solution that takes full advantage of SD card capacity.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] to provide automatic creation of new log files on SD memory, allowing uninterrupted and transparent long-term data collection, especially for sites that are rarely visited.
